# Building Scikit-learn Pipelines

## Overview
As your workflow grows, doing preprocessing steps manually becomes error-prone, and scikit-learn pipelines solve this by chaining every step, scaling, encoding, and the model, into a single object. This matters most for preventing data leakage, one of the most common and dangerous mistakes in data science: if you fit a scaler or imputer on the entire dataset before splitting, information from the test set leaks into training and inflates your scores, giving a false sense of performance. A pipeline ensures each transformation is fit only on training data within each cross-validation fold. The ColumnTransformer lets you apply different preprocessing to different columns (e.g., scale numerics, one-hot encode categoricals) in one step. Pipelines also make hyperparameter tuning clean: GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV can search over both preprocessing and model parameters together. Finally, you can save the entire fitted pipeline with joblib so it can be reused for deployment. Pipelines turn a messy notebook into reproducible, production-ready, leak-free code.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Why pipelines matter; Pipeline and ColumnTransformer; Preventing data leakage; GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV; Saving and loading pipelines (joblib). Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
**Practical Task:** Build a pipeline with a ColumnTransformer that scales numeric and one-hot encodes categorical columns, ends in a classifier, and tune it with GridSearchCV using cross-validation.
**Mini Project:** Refactor an earlier end-to-end model into a single scikit-learn pipeline that handles all preprocessing, is tuned with grid search, and is saved to disk with joblib for reuse.
**Assignment:** Demonstrate data leakage by scaling before vs inside a pipeline and report the difference in cross-validated scores with an explanation.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
